content.comment_body: I created a program for my two [product_name] [article_no] modules. I'm planning to use one as the main unit and the other as secondary, just to get extra I/O. The program is ready, but I can't load it into the [product_name]. I am able to ping the [product_name], but the transfer won't go through. There is no router between my computer and the module, so I can only connect to one [product_name] at a time. Once the program is in the main unit, I will connect the main to the secondary.

Which [product_name] [article_no] model do you have? Is it one of the earlier FS01-FS03 versions, or the newer FS04? If your module is the FS04, you'll need [product_name] [version_no].1. Check this [url] for details: Why can you not download programs into your new [product_name]?
Hello [user_name], what should I do if I have [product_name] [version_no] FS01? Thank you for the explanation.
How am I supposed to know that? What is the exact [article_no] for your [product_name]?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having trouble transferring programs from their computers to [product_name] [article_no] hardware, even though network connectivity has been confirmed by successful pings. The discussion highlights compatibility issues between the hardware versions (such as FS01-FS03 or FS04) and the required [product_name] software versions ([version_no].1). Uncertainty about device [article_no]s and hardware versions adds complexity to finding a solution.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward program transfers from their PC to [product_name] hardware once network connectivity is established. Clear advice regarding compatible hardware and software versions is sought to ensure successful program downloads.
